Verified mechanics: sqlite3_column_table_name yields the origin table for both aliases of a self-join, so both VALUE columns share key 'main_A'; the first read caches the first alias's PK ordinal (via the pkColumns==1 path) and the second alias's blob is opened with the first alias's rowid — silently wrong bytes. Pre-existing in kind (the old single _rowidOrdinal failed the same way), but self-joins sit squarely inside this PR's stated multi-blob-JOIN purpose, so a maintainer reviewing it should know the fix's boundary.

Self-conceded to be outside DbDataReader's documented single-threaded contract; RowIds is an instance field scoped to one query execution (answer-key known_safe confirms no shared state), so the duplicate-key Add throw requires misuse with no concrete in-contract pathway — speculative hardening.
